半原聲吉他（亦稱空心體電吉他）於1930年代出現，目的在提高音量以與鼓等樂器競爭: The semi-acoustic guitar, also called the hollow-body electric guitar, appeared in the 1930s to raise the volume enough to compete with drums and other instruments. In 1936 Gibson brought out its first production model, built with an arched top, soundholes and a single-coil pickup, and its clear sound made it popular with jazz players. In 1949 Gibson introduced a model with a built-in pickup; in 1958 the firm developed the semi-hollow body, using a solid centre block to control feedback, Rickenbacker brought out a wide-body model the same year, and Gretsch models were popular in rockabilly settings.

It was first created in the 1930s and then became popular in jazz and the blues; it is still widely used, and it was also popular in the early days of rock. As rock developed, however, it was largely replaced by the solid-body electric guitar.

電插原聲吉他兼具溫潤與明亮的雙重音色特質。其半空心琴體設計使其具備原聲吉他的共鳴: The electric-acoustic guitar has a double character, warm and bright at once. Its semi-hollow body gives it the resonant warmth of an acoustic guitar, while the electromagnetic pickup captures a clear, penetrating electric sound. The range is wide: the low end resonates fully, the middle is warm and full, and the top has a crystalline sheen. Compared with the cold directness of a solid-body electric guitar, the electric-acoustic has a softer, more human quality; compared with a traditional acoustic guitar its sound carries further and feels more modern. The distinctive hollow-body resonance gives it a natural ring and sustain, so that in jazz and the blues it can shape elegant, expressive phrases, keeping the power of an electric instrument while retaining the warmth of a wooden one.

The neck is normally mahogany and the fretboard ebony or rosewood. The top and back are arched to improve resonance. Inside the electromagnetic pickup are copper coils and neodymium magnets. The strings are usually nickel-wound steel. The machine heads have nickel-alloy gears, and the string pins and strap buttons are nickel silver or nickel-plated brass.
